Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Independent National Electoral Commission has commenced sensitisation of Persons With Disabilities in Adamawa State to enhance their participation in the electoral process. Speaking at a one-day sensitisation workshop in Yola on Monday, the Resident Electoral Commissioner in the state, Nura Mohammed, said the programme was designed to strengthen support for different categories of persons with disabilities and address the barriers they face during elections. Mohammed noted that persons with visual, hearing, physical and other disabilities experienced different challenges and therefore required specific forms of support. He said the workshop would educate participants on physical, information, communication and procedural accessibility, as well as how barriers affected different disability groups. The REC stressed that achieving inclusive elections was not the responsibility of INEC alone, but required collaboration with disability organisations, civil society groups and members of the disability community. He said the workshop would also provide an opportunity for participants to review previous elections, identify gaps and make practical recommendations that could translate into concrete improvements. In his remarks, the Adamawa State Chairman of the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities, Abdullahi Toungo, urged INEC to make adequate provisions for his members to participate effectively in the 2027 general elections. Toungo commended the REC for organising the workshop, saying it would equip participants with information they could take to their respective communities to promote awareness and encourage greater participation in elections. Meanwhile, INEC’s Head of Voter Education and Publicity in Adamawa State, Aliyu Sha’aba, cautioned members of the public against announcing election results before the commission had concluded the voting process. He warned that premature announcements could trigger tension and confusion during elections, urging the public to abide by the commission’s guidelines to prevent disturbances during and after the polls.
